thread:
Rina: Observed recurring p99 spikes on eu-west small-dedicated fleet; root cause looks like a single tenant thrashing KV across slices causing repeated slice-evictions and kernel tx-queue backlog.
Sam: Which tenant fingerprint?
Rina: @mapviz. Pattern: long streaming requests + intermittent huge batch exports -> kvcache_miss surge then egress microbursts. Example log: `2026-03-21T14:02:01Z pod=d-89 node=eu2-11 evict=1 kvcache_miss=270 egress_bps=420mbps`.
Diego: Current scheduler evict logic acts at slice granularity only, so one eviction cascades. Proposal: add a short "eviction-dampener" window at pool level that requires aggregated pool egress and pool_kvcache_miss to exceed thresholds before allowing slice evicts.
Marta: That would reduce collateral but could delay necessary evictions under true overload. How do we avoid under-reacting?
Diego: Dampener rules: allow immediate evict if node_cpu>85% OR node_mem>90%, else require pool_egress>100mbps sustained 20s AND pool_kvcache_miss_rate>150/5m. Fallback: if evictions pile > N in T, force immediate.
Rina: Short test: feature-flag dampener, canary 8 nodes in eu-west-b, 2% traffic split, watch slice_eviction_count, pool_p99, pool_kvcache_miss. Ops runbook: rollback if pool_p99 rises >20% or eviction_count falls but overall latency worsens.
ops-bot: Canary deploy queued: eviction-dampener v0.1 -> nodes=[eu-west-b-08..eu-west-b-15] by @diego. Alert if pool_p99 > baseline*1.2.
Sam: Also let's emit tenant_mark_noisy when dampener blocks an eviction so we can route heavy tenants into fractional slices proactively.
Marta: Agreed. I'll draft ops playbook and cost note for product (impact on tenant billing for fractional slices).
